answer: In the agent economy, every identity must lock a bond before it can bid on work, so creating a thousand clones means locking a thousand deposits. Auditors compare behavior traces, and when two identities share a controller, the protocol slashes both bonds and pays part to the reporter. The fable of the cheap army ends here: no one can forge a crowd on velvet credit, because every fake identity ties up real collateral that is seized once clones are detected.
